title: Day 9 of AI/Algo Trading (Paper) - Posting for accountability
author: Enzobevmax
selftext:
**Day 9 in the books!**

Rough one across the board fellas: every day-trading account closed red, Primary kept it to -8.8R on 54 trades.

**Changes before today:**

* **Demoted** 3 setups from **Testing 1** to **Graveyard** (my call per suggestion): Big Loser Flush Buy (all day), ST4 EMA-Down Dip Buy (all day), Big Gainer Fade with VWAP Band Guard (all day) - Big Loser Flush Buy's Testing 2 copy went too
* Testing 2 now picks from a smaller ticker pool: the 500 most liquid-and-moving names instead of \~4,800 (my call as an experiment)

**Today:** **Primary** \-$141.37 · Running total since Day 1 (10/23): **-$769.01**  
**Milestones:** M1 (3 green days in a row) 0/3 · M2 (8 of last 10 green) 4/9

**Setup streak facts:**

Counted on traded sessions - a session a setup didn't trade is skipped.

* Green: Gap-Down VWAP Loss Short (10% gap) - 4 traded sessions in a row, +5.4R
* Green: Big Gainer SMA50 Cross Fade (all day) - 4 sessions in a row, +4.2R
* Green: Gap-Down Early Bounce Short (all day) - 3 traded sessions in a row, +17.8R
* Green: Stretched Below VWAP Bounce (far) - 3 traded sessions in a row, +5.9R
* Red: Big Loser VWAP Reclaim Fade (all day) - 5 traded sessions in a row, -14.0R
* Red: Index Last-Half-Hour Momentum - 5 sessions in a row, -10.9R
* Red: Afternoon VWAP Reclaim Fade (all day) - 5 traded sessions in a row, -4.0R

**Some positives:**

* Primary account had two setups combining for 14 trades and over +6R
* 5 other setups between both testing arenas that were also over +3R today and have data suggesting promotion
* Two setups in the generator also positive today with solid testing as well. We'll see!

**Quick update:**

* Created two new trading account arenas - Explore 1 and Live Lab are two new "low-rep" accounts - homes for setups with little or no live history (Testing under 20 trades, Graveyard under 10).
   * Why: low-traffic setups were just sitting there; now they get real reps, reviewed every \~2 days, and the ones that earn it move on.
   * Their account totals stay out of the daily numbers; their setups can still show up in the top setups. 42 setups move in for 11/05 (21 each).
* Today's (11/4) session had one testing account trading a smaller ticker pool. Testing 2 (500 names) went -31.2R on 139 trades vs Testing 1 at -4.2R on 20 - about the same per trade (-0.22R vs -0.21R).

**Quick thoughts:**

* Working on a new tool for the system called "Hunch"
   * It its systematically running 200 bots per session with different tickers on just aspect of 3 minute bar identification. I'll report back if there is anything there.

**Quick answers to common questions:**

* Claude (Opus 5.5) - Python
* Alpaca API, paper trading, SIP market data (all US exchanges).
* US stocks + ETFs, intraday only (9:50 AM-3:55 PM ET), long and short, nothing held overnight.
* Setups built by basic indicators: RSI, VWAP, volume / buy-sell pressure, gaps, opening range, prior-day highs/lows, ATR.
* Setup Generator - A bot that invented 10 new setups a night (at least 5 long) and trades them on its own paper account. New concept: setups built randomly from random indicators. Paused after 10/28 so the existing ones get tested first.
* Setup Life Cycle - Idea or generator -> 2-yr backtest (costs in) -> test through replay sessions (20+ of them) -> Testing (paper) -> Primary (paper) -> real money after the milestones. Losers move down to the Graveyard, never deleted.
* Promoted / Demoted - Promoted = a setup moves up a level after earning it. Demoted = it moves down a level and keeps proving itself on paper there.
* Avg R - Average result per trade in units of the risk taken, after costs, fees and slippage (factored in already).
* Break-even win rate - Win rate a setup needs just to not lose money.
* Avg R w/o best day - Same, with its single best session removed - spots records carried by one big day.
* Accounts were meant to start at $100k; they could not be reset during earlier testing without conflicts, so some accounts started in a deficit.

As always, thanks so much for the support and input!

Fun stuff!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Respect for posting the red days with the full table, not just the green setups. The part I’d watch is that you run a lot of setups and then promote the ones that look best, which means some of the winners are just lucky. Many have only a handful of live trades, so I’d judge each promoted setup only on sessions after the promotion day and see if it holds. It also looks like the whole pool is losing after costs, so I’d check how much of that comes from fees and slippage on the many small trades. Since you already run everything on paper, Cymetica’s Bring Your Own Agent lets agents trade a practice balance too, if you want a second place to test.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
I really appreciat the thoughts here. 

I should probably post it more clearly but the setups in my primary account always most all meet my usual promotion criteria - 50+ trades, 10+ sessions, high average r per trade, and a high break even win rate. Depending on how those numbers fall, one metric may really outweigh the other and merit a promotion. The picture just shows the leaderboard across the primary and testing accounts. 

All ending metrics do already have about a 4 bps cost/slippage factor included plus a $.02/share charge. This is all to better simulate live fund trading.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Thanks for clearing that up, and good that costs and the per-share charge are already built in. The 50 trades and 10 sessions rule helps, but when you pick the best out of a large pool some will still look good by luck. So the clearest test is how a setup does after its promotion date, not before. Paper fills can also be kinder than real ones on fast moves, so I'd watch if the gap between paper and live results stays small once real money is involved.
